items.title: Ken Peplowski interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 10, 1997 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] You’ve done some recording with Randy Sandke, right? [INTERVIEWEE] Yeah.

ctx.x: Sometimes you wonder, gee, how come this guy never made a record with that guy — because they’re all stars.

There’s a reason for it. Because they see music differently. They’re band leaders, and they don’t want to work with that person. And unfortunately, the last person that many promoters ask about the music is the musicians. Part of this thing for them is they want to be a band leader. It’s a surrogate thing for them. They can play band leader and put these combinations together. Any time I see the word “all-star” I try to run the other way. Because usually it’s going to be a bunch of guys that are not completely…
If we were to do an interview in ten years, what kind of things would you like me to be able to say that you’ve done?

items.title: Randy Sandke interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 10, 1997
items.q: the first symphony concert that Ken Peplowski and I did we did, I wrote three things

ctx.x: Which shows up on your recent records.

To an extent, although I think the more adventuresome stuff that I’ve done has not been recorded. Some of it I’m starting to. Again, to back up, it’s 1985 when I was working with Benny Goodman and almost all my work was in that swing-Dixieland kind of stuff. I financed my own first record, just saved up I think it was $5,000, and hired, got Mike Brecker and Jim McNealy and John Goldsby, Kenny Washington and did all originals in a modern context. That was my first record. And it got — I still — in some ways I…

wherever it was, whenever it was reviewed. But it led to absolutely nothing in the way of work. No jobs, no nothing. Couldn’t get into clubs, nobody was hiring me as a sideman, nothing, nothing. So I continued working, getting more and more established in this vein, and also traveling to Europe, getting more established over there everywhere as this mainstream trumpet player. Then by the early 90s — so I’m working with like the younger guys I’m working are some of the guys who are here — Ken Peplowski, Howard…
